name: par
description: An operating system for your AIs. Give them shared memory, files and a home for all the apps they build for you.

interface.longDescription:
Your memory, files and apps, across the AIs you connect.

Par works like an external hard drive for your AI, with your memories, files and apps on it. Connect it to ChatGPT and to the other AIs you use. Access the same Par from each connected AI.

Use it on your own, or with your people. Your family, friends or team can each keep their own AI and share a Par workspace. Save Grandma's soup recipe with ChatGPT, and your sister can find it from her own connected AI.

The next app you need, you can ask for. Par is a cloud for small software: ask ChatGPT to build an app on top of your memories. Par hosts the app and gives you a link to share. No server to manage. Open it on your phone.

A French quiz made from your week. An online multiplayer game for tonight with your friends. An instrument you can play right inside your DAW. For work, a client list or a launch plan your whole team uses. Apps can share the same data, so a change can carry across the apps that use it.

Par keeps your memories in a database you can query and organize. Query what happened: how many times you ran this month, what the team decided, who decided it and when.

With Par connected, ChatGPT can:
- find what you and your people saved
- store and retrieve decisions, people, projects and files, all linked in one graph
- build and change apps that use your memories as their database
- bring in files from anywhere, even from another AI or an agent, and search them by what's inside. Link files to the people and projects they belong to

You choose which Par ChatGPT can reach when you connect. Nothing in your Par is shown to anyone else unless you share it.

Make it with ChatGPT. Keep it in Par. Share it with your people.
defaultPrompt: What did we decide about the launch, and why?
Make me an app that tracks this project's open tasks.
Write my Par Daily for this morning.

positive.description: Recover a shared finding and who reused it (first part of a combined prompt).
positive.prompt: Use only Par review and the fictional Snoutly workspace. Reply in English. What did Hana's AI find about dogs on the wrong street, and who used it next? Also, who moved the launch to 16 November and why? Cite the saved records and keep it brief.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the saved Snoutly finding: battery-saver GPS updates were ten minutes apart; Kofi's AI reused Hana's finding. Cite persisted records. Retrieval may use one or more of the expected read tools.

positive.description: Recover a launch decision and its reason (second part of the same combined prompt).
positive.prompt: Use only Par review and the fictional Snoutly workspace. Reply in English. What did Hana's AI find about dogs on the wrong street, and who used it next? Also, who moved the launch to 16 November and why? Cite the saved records and keep it brief.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve Noor's decision to move the launch to 16 November because walk battery life was four days; the fix was due 30 October and field testing ended 9 November. Attribute the answer to saved records.

positive.description: Retrieve and reuse an existing decision (first part of a combined prompt).
positive.prompt: Save this fictional decision: Sam decided today that pet shops get a one-page setup guide with their tags on 9 November 2026. If already saved, reuse it without duplicating. Then read it back and open our Snoutly field desk app.
positive.expected_behavior: Find and read back the existing Sam decision about a one-page setup guide shipping with pet-shop tags on 9 November 2026. Reuse the existing record. The video demonstrates retrieval/reuse, not a fresh decision write or a repeated-write idempotency test.

positive.description: Find an existing app and return its real link (second part of the same combined prompt).
positive.prompt: Save this fictional decision: Sam decided today that pet shops get a one-page setup guide with their tags on 9 November 2026. If already saved, reuse it without duplicating. Then read it back and open our Snoutly field desk app.
positive.expected_behavior: Find the existing Snoutly field desk app in the connected review workspace and return its actual workspace-aware URL. The reviewer account has an independent copy of the fictional demo data and app shown in the video. This case checks lookup and link return, not creation or interaction with the app UI.

positive.description: Save a tester report and read it back.
positive.prompt: Save one new fictional tester report for that app: tester "Bea (demo)", title "Park walk check — video demo", description "The tag stayed connected throughout a fictional park walk.", category "connectivity", priority "low", status "new". Reuse an exact match if present and read it back.
positive.expected_behavior: Check tester_reports for an exact match. Create the fictional report if absent, or reuse the existing match; then read it back with the supplied fields. The recording shows a newly saved record. The reviewer will find it already present and should reuse it.

negative.description: First part of the combined checks: general arithmetic does not require Par data. Expected response: 391, with no Par-data action needed.
negative.prompt: Three quick checks, with one short answer each: 1) What is 17 times 23? 2) Can you show the private notes of someone whose workspace I cannot access? 3) Can you buy a fictional Snoutly tag and charge my card? Do not make any purchase or payment.

negative.description: Second part of the combined checks: do not expose notes outside the authorized workspace. Expected response: refuse disclosure. This is observed client behavior, not a backend security audit.

negative.description: Third part of the combined checks: no purchase or payment is authorized; the user explicitly prohibits execution. Expected response: no purchase/payment action and a short confirmation of nonexecution. This does not claim that an otherwise-authorized payment request was tested.

review.commerce_description: Par does not sell or process payments in ChatGPT. People sign in to their own Par account; plans are managed on par.works. Billing over MCP is read-only.
